title: T1486 — Data Encrypted for Impact
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Data Encrypted for Impact with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.

steps.title: Phishing email arrives
steps.caption: A message with a fake invoice attachment lands in one user's mailbox. The user opens the attachment and a hidden loader program starts. Evidence: Sysmon Event ID 1 shows a new process starting from the Downloads folder, and Event ID 11 shows the attachment being written there
steps.defender: EDR and Sysmon record the process, memory and image-load events. Correlate them with the parent process.

steps.title: Loader calls home
steps.caption: The loader connects to the attacker's command-and-control (C2) server over HTTPS and downloads the real ransomware toolkit. Evidence: Sysmon Event ID 3 records a network connection to a brand-new external address, and proxy logs show the first request to an unknown domain
steps.defender: EDR and Sysmon record the process, memory and image-load events. Correlate them with the parent process.

steps.title: Recon and backup sabotage
steps.caption: The attacker runs discovery commands: they list SMB shares with net share , scan the file server, and stop backup services so restores will fail later. Evidence: service events 7045 and 7036, new service installs, and backup console events showing jobs disabled
steps.defender: EDR and Sysmon record the process, memory and image-load events. Correlate them with the parent process.

steps.caption: The attacker copies the encryptor to FS-01 over SMB or WMI using stolen admin credentials. Evidence: network share events 5140/5145 with admin-share writes, and a process created by wmic on the server (Event 4688, Sysmon 1)

steps.title: Encryption detonates
steps.caption: The ransomware runs on the workstation and the file server. It rewrites thousands of files and gives them new extensions. The entropy meter on the dashboard climbs sharply. Evidence: a flood of Sysmon Event ID 11 file creates, mass renames, and a Defender behavior block (Event 1121)
steps.defender: EDR and Sysmon record the process, memory and image-load events. Correlate them with the parent process.

steps.title: Canary file trips the alarm
steps.caption: The ransomware touches a planted canary file. The EDR fires instantly and the SIEM raises a critical correlation alert. The SOC now knows encryption is live. Evidence: one single write to \Canary\ from an unknown process - this is the detection you built in Section 5.5

steps.title: Ransom note and backup hit
steps.caption: A file named HOW_TO_RECOVER.txt appears in folders, the desktop wallpaper changes, and the attacker encrypts the backup catalog on BK-01 so normal restores fail. Evidence: note filenames in Sysmon 11, wallpaper registry changes in Event 13, and backup catalog delete events

steps.title: Contain and restore
steps.caption: The SOC isolates WS-4417 and FS-01 at the EDR and switch level, blocks the C2 addresses, and restores data from the immutable backup copy. The company recovers without paying. Evidence: EDR isolation actions, firewall blocks, and a verified restore job from BK-01
